items.title: Bob Wilber interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, May 22, 1998
items.q: [(note)] Bob was interviewed at Hamilton on May 22, 1998, by Monk Rowe, Director of the Hamilton College Jazz Archive.

ctx.x: Bob Wilber was born in New York City on March 15, 1928. He began performing professionally while still in high school, playing clarinet and saxophone and leading The Wildcats. Bob became a protégé of Sidney Bechet and is a leading exponent of classic jazz on the soprano sax and clarinet. His extensive list of recordings include collaborations with Kenny Davern, Teddy Wilson and Dick Wellstood. He is a prolific composer and arranger and has produced critically acclaimed tribute albums highlighting the music of…
Bob was interviewed at Hamilton on May 22, 1998, by Monk Rowe, Director of the Hamilton College Jazz Archive.

We are filming for the Hamilton College Jazz Archive on the Hamilton campus today. It’s a great pleasure for me to have saxophonist, clarinetist, arranger, composer, and on the eve of receiving an honorary degree of Hamilton, Bob Wilber.
